title: Polynomial-time detection below the planted-clique square-root threshold
decision_reason: Exact formulation, independent corroboration, current searches, theorem-scope comparisons, baseline distinctness and separate adversarial draft review passed; awaits batch integration and prepublication refresh.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: One observed labeled simple undirected graph
problem_fingerprint.domain: All graphs on [n], sampled under P0 or P1
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every epsilon and every randomized polynomial-time algorithm, liminf risk >= 1
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Risk is Type I plus Type II error; balanced-prior accuracy = 1-risk/2
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Fix epsilon and algorithm, then n -> infinity
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Classical randomized polynomial time in adjacency-matrix input size, not a restricted algorithm family; conjecture itself is an unconditional hardness assertion

statement_source_and_scope_match: BBH Conjecture 1 and HMP Conjecture 4 include this fixed power-law sequence and edge probability 1/2. The statement concerns detection with nonvanishing advantage, not recovery or negligible advantage.
proposed_statement_text: For every fixed epsilon in (0,1/2), let k_n=floor(n^(1/2-epsilon)), P0=G(n,1/2) and P1=P0 with all missing edges added within an independent uniformly chosen k_n-subset. Does every randomized polynomial-time detection algorithm A satisfy liminf_n [P0(A=1)+P1(A=0)] >= 1?
applied_significance: A basic model for detecting a dense anomalous group in a noisy network; also a hypothesis underlying average-case reductions for statistical-computational gaps, including submatrix detection and sparse inference.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: No existing or accepted candidate has these null/alternative distributions and detection-hardness target.
implications_or_equivalences: Do not add recovery or other equivalent planted-clique formulations as separate counts.

open_status_evidence_summary: Explicit decision conjecture in BBH and HMP; independent HS treats it as a hardness conjecture while proving reductions. April 2026 ABML introduction still distinguishes restricted lower bounds from an unknown general barrier.
independent_status_corroboration: HS has no authors in common with BBH/HMP. ABML independently describes the unresolved general Erdős–Rényi barrier in its April 2026 version.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: Polynomial-time recovery at constant multiples of sqrt(n); known algorithm-class lower bounds do not cover all randomized polynomial-time algorithms.

issues_found: Vanishing advantage must not be confused with nonvanishing advantage.
Fixed-k, binomial-k and adversarial-k variants have different direct formulations.
Degree-limited SoS is not all polynomial time.
issues_resolved: Kept p=1/2 and fixed floor(n^(1/2-epsilon)) from the exact sequence conjecture.
Risk and equal-prior accuracy normalized consistently; constant versus vanishing advantage explicit.
Used independent HS and ABML for status, not as a substitute for the exact fixed-k source.
Hypothesis-by-hypothesis algorithm comparisons in ledger; no unsupported network-performance claim.
